title: The Form pattern can never show the error states its specification documents
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, asked to recommend how the patterns should be tested
details:
`FormDemo` marks its fields `required` through FormGroup and submits to its own `handleSubmit`, which calls a `validate()` and sets an `error` on each group. The form carries no `noValidate`.

FormGroup forwards `required` to the child input, which is documented and right on its own. The browser then refuses to fire submit on an invalid form, so `handleSubmit` never runs, `validate()` never runs, no `error` is ever set, and the `role="alert"` branch is unreachable. The user sees the browser's own bubble instead of the design system's error treatment.

`patterns/Form.md` documents error states the pattern cannot reach, and the screenshot gate photographs the never-erroring form as correct.

The fix is a judgement call worth making deliberately rather than quickly. Adding `noValidate` to the demo's form is the smallest change and is what a consumer doing its own validation has to do. Dropping `required` would lose the accessible marking. Either way the lesson belongs in `patterns/Form.md`, because a consumer copying this pattern inherits the same silent failure: native constraint validation and custom validation do not compose without `noValidate`.

notes.text: Reported by a reviewer with no context on this repository's recent work, then reproduced here independently rather than taken on trust. A form with one required FormGroup and a submit handler records 0 handler calls and 0 elements with role alert after the submit button is clicked. Confirmed at source: FormGroup.tsx:72-74 forwards required, and FormDemo.tsx:46 has no noValidate.
This is the class of defect the visual gate cannot see, and it is the second one found this way. A form that never errors looks identical to a form that has not been submitted.
